claims.claim: The no-argument diagnostic fixes execution to one exact serial target subprocess followed by one independent n4/load target-file subprocess, without retries or fallback phases.
The target-only probe delegates each observed PUSH once with unchanged arguments and options, retaining only bounded outcomes, return codes, allowlisted stderr categories and path lengths.
The diagnostic separately records serial target outcome, n4 target outcome and n4 non-target failure count, and selects exactly one prescribed observational classification.
The implementation rejects subject changes, dirty worktrees, invalid target or worker identities, inconsistent reports, invalid lock-path lengths, malformed schemas and over-bound observations.
Added regression cases cover all classifications and stderr categories, exact-once delegation, operand redaction, argument rejection, observation bounds and subject mutation rejection.
The committed change contains only the three permitted diagnostic files and leaves existing fixtures, tests, production code and lifecycle surfaces unchanged.
